Figure 1. Study design, core Mendelian randomization assumptions, and endpoint hierarchy. Abbreviations: MR, Mendelian randomization; IVs, instrumental variables; SNPs, single-nucleotide polymorphisms; IVDD, intervertebral disc disorders; UKB, UK Biobank; CAD, coronary artery disease.

Figure 2. Inverse-variance weighted MR estimates across the endpoint hierarchy. Shaded bands distinguish registry, symptom, exploratory, sensitivity, and systemic-comparison outcomes. Abbreviations: IVW, inverse-variance weighted; OR, odds ratio; CI, confidence interval; CAD, coronary artery disease.

Figure 3. Alternative adiposity and UK Biobank body-composition sensitivity analyses. The heatmap and forest plot show IVW estimates for registry-based outcomes. Stars indicate P-value categories. Abbreviations: WHR, waist-to-hip ratio; UKB, UK Biobank.
Figure 4. Evidence triangulation across primary and sensitivity analyses. Each row links the empirical result to its interpretation and principal limitation.

Figure 5. Conceptual pathways linking adiposity and smoking liability to degenerative spine outcomes. Solid arrows indicate biologically plausible pathways, whereas dashed arrows indicate indirect or uncertain pathways. The schematic does not represent a mediation analysis.

Figure 6. Sensitivity assessment of the four primary exposure-outcome pairs. Status markers summarize directionality, estimator concordance, Steiger, leave-one-out, MR-PRESSO, MRlap, and MVMR findings. Abbreviations: LOO, leave-one-out; MVMR, multivariable Mendelian randomization.

Figure 7. Integrated interpretation of the endpoint-hierarchy MR evidence. Registry-based outcomes anchor the primary interpretation, whereas symptom and systemic outcomes define its boundaries. The schematic does not represent a mediation model.
Figure 8. Evidence architecture and interpretive boundaries. The diagram distinguishes study design, quantitative results, sensitivity analyses, biological interpretation, and clinical translation.

Figure 9. Estimator concordance for the four primary exposure-outcome pairs. IVW odds ratios and 95% confidence intervals are shown; weighted-median and MR-Egger results are displayed as point estimates because full confidence intervals were unavailable in the summarized results.

Figure 10. Diagnostic summary for the four primary exposure-outcome pairs. Status indicators summarize heterogeneity, MR-Egger intercept, MR-PRESSO outlier, Steiger, NOME, and leave-one-out findings. MR-PRESSO is treated as auxiliary sensitivity evidence.

Figure 11. Exploratory sample-overlap scenario analysis. This proxy analysis illustrates sensitivity to hypothetical overlap; it is not a formal pair-specific correction and did not inform the primary conclusions.

Figure 12. Multivariable MR sensitivity analysis for BMI and smoking initiation. Panel A compares univariable IVW estimates with mutually adjusted estimates. Panel B shows conditional-F sensitivity across assumed constant cross-exposure estimation-error correlations from rho = -0.90 to 0.90. BMI remained above the conventional F = 10 threshold throughout the grid, whereas smoking initiation remained below it. The grid is a covariance-assumption stress test and does not estimate the true covariance. Abbreviations: BMI, body mass index; IVDD, intervertebral disc disorders; IVW, inverse-variance weighted; MVMR, multivariable Mendelian randomization.

Figure 13. Observed and MRlap-corrected standardized estimates for the four primary pairs. MRlap estimates are standardized sensitivity measures and were not exponentiated or interpreted as primary odds ratios.

Figure 14. Data requirements for sex-specific MR. Matched sex-specific exposure and outcome summary statistics were unavailable; therefore, no sex-specific causal estimates or sex-difference claims are reported.
